item: 2017 NFL Personnel (Injury) Report Policy PDF

Consequently this site does not quote the policy text and does not assert what 'Questionable' or 'Doubtful' officially mean. Only the categories observed on the live report are recorded.
action: No definition text published. Category labels reproduced exactly as observed.

item: League-wide depth charts page
detail: https://www.nfl.com/depth-charts/ returns HTTP 404. There is no league-wide official depth chart at that address. All depth information on this site therefore comes from club sites or from roster status codes, and is labelled DERIVED.
action: Depth presented as a derived layer only, never as official.

item: Football Operations injury-report landing page
detail: https://operations.nfl.com/health-safety/injury-report/ returns HTTP 404. An official policy landing page could not be located at this path.
action: None. Recorded for completeness.

item: Myles Garrett — club attribution
detail: NFL.com's Week 10 injury report lists Myles Garrett as an LB on the Los Angeles Rams with a knee designation and a 'resting player' note. NFL.com's Next Gen Stats front page carries a 2026 Rams article titled 'Rams' Sean McVay: No timeline on Myles Garrett's return post knee surgery', and a separate NFL.com article is headlined 'How does Myles Garrett fit into Rams defense?'. These agree on the Rams but the injury-row note mixes a real knee injury with a rest designation, which the site will not attempt to untangle. No resolution applied.
action: Row published verbatim as captured. Both sources linked.

item: Aaron Donald — listed as a non-participant while shown as active
detail: The Week 10 Rams injury table lists Aaron Donald (DT) as 'Did Not Participate In Practice' with no injury and no game status. NFL.com's own player profile for Aaron Donald shows him as an active Los Angeles Rams DE with 11 years of experience, and an NFL.com article states he unretired on Aug. 30 and planned a season debut. Both are official NFL.com pages and they cannot both be read at face value. No resolution applied.
action: Row published verbatim. Profile linked alongside.

item: Four clubs absent from the Week 10 injury snapshot
detail: The captured Week 10 injury report covers 28 of 32 clubs. Chicago, Denver, Tampa Bay and Philadelphia are absent. All 28 clubs that do appear also appear in the 14-game Week 10 schedule capture. Whether those four clubs are on a bye or their reports were simply not posted at capture time could not be confirmed, because no official 2026 bye-week table was verified in this session.
action: Counts are always stated as 'x of 28 captured clubs', never as a league total.

item: One Week 10 game was already final at capture time
detail: Washington at New York Giants kicked off Thursday 2026-11-12 and finished 24-21. Their injury tables are still shown in the Week 10 report. Using those rows as a pre-game signal would be look-ahead bias. They are the completed game's report, not a forecast input.
action: Flagged so no analysis treats the completed game's rows as forward-looking.

item: No benchmark price source exists in this repository
detail: The league publishes results, statistics and schedules but not betting prices. No odds feed, historical closing line, or graded result set is present or was licensed for this session. Every edge, expected-value and closing-line-value field on this site is therefore blank. Nothing has been estimated or imputed to fill them.
action: All price, edge and EV fields left blank and labelled. See question Q03 and suggestion SG01.

item: No official snap counts available
detail: Determining that a second- or third-string player actually replaced a starter requires snap share. No snap-count feed was located or verified. The deficiency model therefore reports official absence designations only, and does not claim that any specific backup played.
action: Deficiency magnitude left blank. See question Q05 and suggestion SG04.

item: Club depth charts are self-described as unofficial
detail: The one club depth chart captured in full is headed 'Kansas City Chiefs Unofficial Depth Chart' by the club itself. Its ordering is reproduced exactly, but it is not an official league ranking and must not be presented as one.
action: Labelled DERIVED / UNOFFICIAL wherever it appears.

item: Player-name collisions make name joins unsafe
detail: Two different players named Marcus Harris appear in the captured data: a Tennessee cornerback and a Kansas City defensive tackle. NFL player URLs disambiguate them with numeric suffixes, but plain names do not. Any join performed on player name alone will silently merge distinct people.
action: Rows kept separate. Any future join must key on the player URL, not the display name.

item: Legal and regulatory sources not verified
detail: No gambling-regulator, tax or gaming-commission source was loaded or verified during this session. The site therefore makes no statement about legality, licensing or tax treatment in any jurisdiction, including the user's location. Nothing on this site is a bet, an offer to wager, or bookmaking.
action: Legal question recorded as open (Q14) and left unanswered. Leaderboard rewards kept non-monetary (SG11).

item: Terms of use for automated fetching not reviewed
detail: Every capture in this session was a single page load. The terms of use and robots policy of nfl.com and of the 32 club sites were not reviewed, so no statement is made about whether scheduled automated collection would be permitted.
action: No scheduled collector was built. See question Q18.

item: Single-season, single-snapshot dataset
detail: All data here comes from one 2026 season and, for injuries, one capture on one day. Nothing on this site has a multi-season history, so no claim of persistence over time can be made and no backtest has been run.
action: Every strategy is marked NOT RUN or BLOCKED. No performance figure is displayed.

item: A parallel session's injury CSV had a column-shift bug on multi-injury cells
detail: A concurrent session independently transcribed the same Week 10 report into data/injuries.csv. Comparing the two transcriptions row by row: all 161 rows it contains also appear in this repo's 345-row capture, with no row present only in theirs. 156 of 161 rows match field for field, which is a useful independent confirmation of the capture. The 5 that differed all involve a player with two listed body parts: 'Ankle, Knee', 'Wrist, Chest', 'Knee, Achilles', 'Ankle, Triceps' and 'Ankle, Knee'. Because that CSV was comma-delimited and the injury field was unquoted, the second body part shifted into the adjacent columns, so the practice and game status fields were displaced. This repo's capture preserves the full published value and the correct game status, and the raw page capture confirms it (e.g. A.J. Brown 'Ankle, Knee / Limited Participation / Questionable').
action: This repo keeps its own capture, which was verified line by line against the raw page. The other session's files are preserved in archive/v2/ for reference. Any future CSV export must quote every field containing a comma.

item: Houston Texans depth chart published as an image
detail: https://www.houstontexans.com/team/depth-chart loads, but the chart itself is rendered as an image inside a photo-gallery widget rather than as a position table. No player names are machine-readable. Houston is therefore the only club of 32 with no depth chart on this site. The Texans roster page does publish a readable table, but it is ordered alphabetically, not by depth, so it cannot be substituted without inventing the string ordering. Depth is an ordering, and the ordering is the fact being reported.
action: Houston is absent from the Backup Depth page and counted as uncovered. Nothing inferred in its place.

item: Player-prop correlations are computed estimates from a third-party mirror
detail: data/prop-correlations-d.csv coefficients are computed from nflverse player_stats 1999-2024 via the Beexly/Sports mirror (file commit 2026-11-07), QA-gated (schema, coverage, 100% score join vs games.csv, distribution sanity, deterministic rebuild). The source parquet is not committed and its prior workspace-only path is absent from this checkout; therefore the prop-correlation rebuild check V9 is BLOCKED here. The existing coefficients remain third-party-derived and were not independently regenerated in this run.
action: Retain the third-party label; for reproducible refreshes, fetch a pinned source artifact and record its content hash. Until that input and QA run are available, treat V9 as BLOCKED and do not claim this checkout independently reproduced the estimates.

item: Betting prices, opening and closing lines, for every market we originate (side, total, moneyline)
detail: No official NFL source publishes betting lines or closing prices (GAP-01; Q-02). The price-snapshot store (data/price_snapshots.tsv) therefore holds no prices. The market and difference columns in data/model_lines.tsv are blank, and so is the ROI column in the backtest. Third-party prices exist in data/raw/closing_lines.csv (nflverse) and were not promoted.
action: Owner decision needed: an official or licensed price feed, or an explicit decision to accept a third-party feed as a labelled non-official source. Until then every market cell stays blank.

item: Correlation values computed from nflverse / third-party data (prop correlations; C-01 measured rho)
detail: Brief B6 requires correlations to be computed only from officially sourced numbers, with n published. The prop-correlation values (for example QB pass yards vs WR receiving yards r = 0.7887, n = 5,246; QB vs TE r = 0.3729, n = 5,208; RB rush vs RB receive r = 0.3562, n = 5,246, and the 2022-2024 window values) and the measured C-01 rho = +0.00696 (95% CI -0.03324 to +0.04831, n = 6,813) come from the third-party nflverse mirror. They are withheld from the root site and the measured page carries a withdrawal banner. n is kept for each pair. The withheld values are reproduced here for review only. RESOLVED-IN-PART 2026-11-14 (session arena-5876146b-fl1): official-only correlations now published with n at official-correlations.html (C-O1 r=+0.076 n=137; C-O2/C-O3 |r|<0.09 n=242). The third-party prop-correlation values remain withheld as stated.
action: partially closed by official-correlations.html; third-party values stay withheld (F-11)

kind: Model does not beat a constant benchmark out of sample
item: Own-line fair model (side, total) backtest, weeks 4-10 of 2026
detail: Walk-forward, strictly out of sample, n = 89 games. Side: model MAE 10.49 vs constant league-average benchmark 10.33 points; sign accuracy 67.0% (95% Wilson CI 56.7%-76.0%, n = 88). Total: model MAE 11.07 vs constant 10.96 points. Moneyline Brier 0.2181 vs 0.2472 for a 50/50 forecast. The fair lines are published as model output only. They are not a validated edge, there is no market baseline, and ROI cannot be computed (F18).
action: Do not treat the fair lines as a recommendation. Review the calibration table before any further model work; a larger sample (more seasons of official results) is needed before any margin claim.

kind: Assumption: home-field term at the Munich game
item: Patriots at Lions, 15 Nov 2026, Munich
detail: The official Week 10 page labels this game an 'International Game' played in Munich, Germany, and lists it as 'Patriots at Lions'. The model sets the home-field term to zero for this game. That is an assumption made by this session, not an official fact. The neutral-venue flag for the 137 results comes from the third-party schedule feed (data/schedule2026-d.csv).
action: Confirm the venue convention for the fair line. The effect is at most the home-field estimate of about 0.05 points on the fitted model.

item: 137 results in data/results.tsv used as model inputs
detail: Per-game scores were re-read from an official page only for Week 10 (Commanders 24, Giants 21, FINAL). RESOLVED 2026-11-14 (session arena-5876146b-fl1): every one of the 137 finals is now verified per-game against the official nfl.com week pages (row-level capture raw/official-finals-2026.tsv; three-way check scripts/verify_feed_m.py 137/137 PASS). The aggregate-only status applied to weeks 1-9 no longer holds.
action: closed — row-level official capture supersedes aggregate reconciliation

item: Market prices are third-party only - no official league source prices NFL lines
detail: Requirement R24 mandates publishing the market-line and difference columns; the standing verification rule says leave unconfirmed values blank. Provisional resolution applied in this sprint: market cells are transcribed from the sha256-pinned nflverse capture (S47) and badged THIRD_PARTY; difference cells inherit the badge. The strict-blank alternative is one edit away and is left open as question Q23 (the old F-11 decision, now unavoidable).
action: Review Q23 / SG24. Option B switches every market cell to blank.

item: Root Leaderboard page claimed no backtest existed anywhere in the repository while the computed layer publishes 16 backtested strategies
detail: strategies.html carried the sentence 'No backtest has been executed and no performance figure is claimed anywhere in this repository', but data/leaderboard.csv and docs/pages/ carry 16 strategies backtested over third-party data (2006-2026). The two registers answer different questions (official-data plan vs third-party research), but 'anywhere' was false. The sprint section on the Leaderboard page now states the split; the original sentence is preserved there as the plan-level register's statement about official data.

item: Moneyline opening and closing prices are not captured for the Week 10 slate
detail: The price-snapshot store holds MONEYLINE-HOME and MONEYLINE-AWAY rows for all 14 games with every price cell blank: the Week 10 board captures spread and total only, and closing_lines.csv carries moneyline prices only for 2006-2025 (third-party). Nothing was inferred to fill them.
action: Q22: approve a moneyline capture source.

item: week10_signal_board.csv 'closing_spread_home' holds the AWAY team's spread, and 'market_implied_home_winprob' comes from an unvalidated formula
detail: Check V8 (data/verification-d.tsv) verified across 13/13 games that nflverse spread_line is the away team's point spread, so the board's column name is wrong for its content. market_implied_home_winprob = logistic(0.28 * spread_line) has no cited basis and behaves like a probability of the away side's margin, not a home win probability; it is excluded from the line board and the price store. The line board negates the verbatim value into home view and says so per row; the store keeps the verbatim number as the AWAY quote.
action: SG26: annotate columns and add a derived home-view column; do not rename.

item: Origination order mandated: side first, then total, then moneyline - supersedes the earlier totals-first note
detail: data/models.json described the architecture as 'deliberately totals-first'. Requirement R23 fixes the order SIDE, then TOTAL, then MONEYLINE. The pipeline, the snapshot store and the line board now follow the mandated order. The old wording is preserved in this flag so the change is visible rather than silent.
action: None - recorded so the change is auditable.

item: Demotion-gate thresholds are proposed competition rules, not measured facts
detail: G-14 (engine/demotion.py) uses D1 window=100 settled bets with inferiority alpha 0.10, D2 max drawdown 25 flat-stake units, D3 trailing CLV rot, and re-promotion after 300 fresh settled bets at the G-2b standard. These are constructor arguments chosen as a design decision; a reviewer may change them. What cannot be changed by review is the verdict logic: DEMOTE cannot be reinterpreted as HOLD.
action: Q24: confirm or revise the thresholds.

item: Fair-line coefficients are computed from the 2026 official feeds only (137 games)
detail: Home-field advantage -0.022 points per game and margin sd 13.225 points are computed by engine/fairline.py from data/results.tsv (S52) as of 2026-11-14; the strength convention (PF-PA)/G with a /2 meeting rule is a published bookkeeping choice, not a fitted coefficient. No coefficient is tuned on market prices. The 2026 home-field estimate being ~0 is a property of this season's 137 games, not a claim about the NFL.
action: Q26: schedule out-of-sample refits after two official seasons.

item: Computed-layer leaderboard's breakeven_hit is circular: 1/(1+realized ROI), not the price hurdle
detail: scripts/strategy_lab.py computes avg_dec as the mean of (realized profit/stake + 1) over settled bets - losers contribute 0 - so breakeven_hit = 1/(1+realized ROI) and gate G4 ('beats_vig') is tested against a quantity derived from the outcomes being tested. Every spread strategy at ordinary prices is then failed by construction (e.g. WIND15_UNDER: breakeven_hit 0.9326 = 1/1.0724 = 1/(1+ROI 0.0723)). The per-bet odds ARE present in that pipeline's bet ledger (home_spread_odds etc.), so the correct price-based hurdle is computable there with a one-line fix. Nothing in the computed layer was edited by this session; the value is transcribed as dataset_breakeven_hit_transcribed in data/leaderboard_signal_staking.json and NOT used for ranking - the signal split ranks against the standard -110 reference hurdle instead and labels it.
action: SG28: recompute breakeven from per-bet odds in the computed layer and re-run its gates; until then treat its G4 column as unusable.

item: Two parallel sessions implemented the same eight requirements (R21-R28); both implementations are preserved
detail: Session arena/685f958d-fl1 (PRs #22-#32, merged first) and session arena-360ca650-fl1 (this merge) each built a price store, results feed, line model, signal/staking split, availability/replacement tracking, correlation policy and a demotion gate. Nothing was discarded. The divergences are substantive and left for the owner: (1) MARKET-PRICE POLICY - model-lines.html keeps every market/difference cell blank (no official price source), while line-board.html publishes the pinned third-party capture with a THIRD_PARTY badge and a per-row convention note (see Q23); (2) DEMOTION SEMANTICS - the D1-D3 gate (CLV decay, calibration drift, concentration) and the G-14 gate (signal decay, drawdown, CLV rot; 300-bet re-promotion) define different triggers and thresholds (see Q24); (3) duplicate pages: results-feed.html (arena/685f958d) vs verified-results-feed.html (arena/360ca650), line-board.html vs model-lines.html, plus two price stores (data/price_snapshots.tsv vs data/price_snapshots.json). Cross-links connect each pair. A THIRD parallel implementation (session arena-5876146b-fl1, tasks M1-M8) landed the same eight requirements alongside R21-R28 and the arena/685f958d-fl1 work. Final integration preserved all three: duplicate pages cross-linked (results-feed.html is the merged superset; verified-results-feed.html and the R21-R28 registers stay), and colliding ids were re-issued for the third set: sources S61-S69, flags F32-F36, governance gates G-16/G-17 (renamed from this branch's G-14/G-15 to clear their G-14 in validation_gates.json).
action: reconciled at final integration; all three implementations preserved and cross-linked

action: owner review: reword D2 or restate the origination order there

The total market columns (fair | market | difference) are published as structure with the fair and difference cells empty. Filling them requires the official drive/efficiency inputs (GAP-05) and a fitted model. Distinct from F19 (which withholds third-party correlation values). see also F29 (fair-line provenance) and F25.

detail: Every market column (spread, total, moneyline) behind the fair-line comparison comes from data/raw/games.csv (nflverse/nfldata, S47), flagged third-party. A licensed/official price feed landing behind the price-snapshot store is the only way past this (Q-02). See also F18 (same gap registered by the price-store session). same gap registered as F23 by the R21-R28 sprint.

detail: data/replacement_depth.csv derives each replacement from official inputs (Week 10 injury report S01 + club depth charts) using the published rule: first listed player at the same spot whose official game status is not Out; string = published rank. Houston has no machine-readable chart (F16) so no rows exist for it. Six spots show every listed player Out — those replacement cells are blank and flagged, never filled. One NE RB replacement comes from 3rd string with one player Out above him.

item: requirements.txt declares stdlib-only while scripts/ require pandas, numpy and scipy
detail: engine/ and tools/ are standard-library only as documented. scripts/ (strategy_lab.py, fetch_data.py, and session M's builders) require pandas/numpy/scipy — this was already true before this session; the requirements note understates it. The store (engine/price_snapshots.py) records both phases, but no verified opener source exists in this repository: the third-party games snapshot holds closing/latest values only, and the historical closing-lines file covers 2006-2025 with closes and no 2026 rows. Every open_* cell on price-snapshots.html is therefore blank. An opener inferred from a close would be a fabrication.  Cross-reference: (overlaps F23/F25: price sources)

item: A quarter of the backtest log is priced at an assumed -110 because the feed carries a line with no odds

detail: Week 11 (2026-11-19/22) has 16 games and none has a spread, total or moneyline in the capture; the whole season has 272 games of which 234 are lined. item: The 2026 season in the captured feed stops at Week 9 plus one Week 10 game, and the official standings row for 2026 shows 16-1
detail: data/results.tsv (transcribed from the official Week-by-week pages, S04/S49) contains 137 games: weeks 1-4 have 16 games, weeks 5 and 9 have 15, weeks 6-8 have 14, week 10 has 1. item: No bet in this repository can be measured for closing-line value, so the promotion gate that needs CLV cannot run and no reward can be paid
detail: CLV needs the price at the time the pick was made and the close after it. The capture has no dated open, so 0 of 13,310 bets are measurable. This session's demotion run therefore evaluates D1 against the recorded market line as a named substitute (D1-SUBSTITUTE) and reports the substitution on the page rather than presenting it as the original rule.
action: demotion-gate.html publishes the substitute definition, the numbers, and the exact unlock (the snapshot collector). Rewards: 0 units paid, 9 of 9 rules ineligible - stated on signal-vs-staking.html.

item: The model's own signal is negative against the market on all three markets, and worse as the threshold tightens
detail: Walk-forward, 2011-2026, 13,310 bets: side rules lose 1.98 to 4.96 points per bet vs the recorded market line (3,364 bets at a 1.0-point gap), and both total rules are inverted - calibration slope -0.02 to -0.07, i.e. a bigger stated gap predicts a worse result. Moneyline rules are -0.017 to -0.020 probability points.
action: Published as the headline of the leaderboard rather than hidden in a footnote; nothing is promoted, so nothing is exposed to the negative edge. The tuning grid that chose these parameters is published with the model card.

item: Three of the four line files have no field documentation at all - only filenames assert what they are
detail: Upstream DATASETS.md documents the games feed (result = home-away; total = sum; spread_line positive = home favoured) and does not document closing_lines.csv, sc_lines.csv, initial_lines.csv or win_totals.csv. The publisher's own code (code/draft_kings.R) scrapes live DraftKings prices for unplayed games, which explains current-season movement but is not documentation of the historical columns. No CRAN reference page for these functions is reachable.
action: The store records the vintage claim as 'filename only' in the vintage_evidence column of every snapshot row, and pages print UNDOCUMENTED rather than guessing a market hour.

item: This session refreshed one capture, and the diff is 26 fields - all moneylines of games that have not been played
detail: data/raw/games.csv at main was 9 days behind upstream. 7,548 games on both sides, 0 added or removed; the difference is 26 rows' moneyline columns (13 games x 2 sides), e.g. 2026_10_HOU_CLE home moneyline -230 -> -225. Scores, spreads and totals are unchanged, so no historical settlement in this repository moves.
action: Refreshed file committed with its new sha256 in the manifest and the previous hash recorded alongside it, so the change is auditable rather than silent.

item: Week 10 injury row count: the review says 254 rows published against 279 live; both of this session's official reads are larger
detail: An earlier review recorded the published injury table as 254 rows and the live page as 279 rows, with four 'no injuries reported' sections. This session read the same official URL twice: the 2026-11-14 capture in the repository parses to 345 rows across 28 clubs, and a fresh 2026-11-16 re-capture parses to 347 rows across the same 28 clubs, with no 'no injuries reported' section on the page in either read. Both raw captures are committed with sha256 hashes so the discrepancy can be re-checked line by line. No number was altered to make the figures agree.
action: Both dated captures published on the Snapshot Ledger page with their hashes; the diff between them is published too. The 254/279 figures could not be reproduced and are left as recorded, not corrected.

kind: Not found in an official source
item: Announced-starter evidence for Brissett (Arizona) — named in the brief, not found on any official page read
detail: The brief lists Brissett among the starters the NFL has announced. The dated official roundup of 2026-11-11 announces Carson Beck as Arizona's Week 10 starter, and Brissett appears on neither the Week 10 injury report nor any article read this session. The cell is left blank on the Announced Starters page with this reason, rather than filled from a depth chart or from memory.
action: Row published blank with the reason and the source link. If an official page naming Brissett exists, the fix is to add the link.

kind: Source changed between two dated reads
item: The official Week 10 injury report is not a single fact: it moved between 2026-11-14 and 2026-11-16
detail: Re-reading nfl.com/injuries two days later returned 347 rows where the earlier read had 345. Two rows were added (BAL Calais Campbell, BAL Ronnie Stanley) and 32 fields moved. 22 of the 32 are Chargers rows: Los Angeles played on Monday night, so its game-day designations were published after the earlier read. Indianapolis's Arden Key moved the other way — Questionable with a hamstring injury on 11-14, no designation at all on 11-16.
action: The 2026-11-14 read is kept as the pre-kickoff snapshot and is never overwritten; the later read is published beside it with a diff. Backtests must pin the capture they used.

item: The depth-chart register carries no capture date on 31 of 31 rows
detail: data/depth-sources.tsv records club, source id and URL for 31 clubs, but its chartDate column is empty on every row. Without a capture date, a depth chart cannot be checked for staleness against the roster events the brief asks us to track, and two captures of the same chart are indistinguishable.
action: Register left as-is with the gap stated; filling the column is requirement R62 on the backlog. No date was invented.

item: Venue, roof and surface are captured only from a third-party feed; the official transcription covers 1 of 272 fixtures
detail: data/schedule2026-d.csv carries stadium, roof and surface for all 272 games, but every one of those rows is attributed to a third-party aggregation. The official schedule transcription in data/schedule.tsv has a venue on 1 row of 272 (the Munich international game). The brief asks for the venue to be transcribed from the official game centre.
action: Third-party venue fields are recorded in the store with their provenance label and are not presented as official. Official transcription is requirement R43 on the backlog.

item: Published model outputs record a line, not a probability with its input vector
detail: The brief asks that every model output be stored as a probability plus the inputs that produced it. The current origination artefacts store a fair line and a difference column, and the fair column is blank because the model is unfitted (F38). Even when fitted, a line without its input vector cannot be audited or reproduced after the fact.
action: Recorded as requirement R35 on the backlog with the schema change it needs. No output was retro-fitted to look complete.

item: The published standings and results predate eleven finals that the official site has since published
detail: data/standings.tsv and data/results.tsv were captured on 2026-11-14 and hold 137 results. Reading the official league standings page and the official Week 10 schedule page on 2026-11-16 returned eleven further finals, taking the season to 148 results, and the standings had moved accordingly (for example Miami and Tennessee from 1-7 to 1-8, Kansas City from 6-2 to 7-2). The newer read was transcribed and reconciled: it reproduces the newer standings for all 32 clubs on W, L, T, PF and PA (check G-R1). The frozen corpus was NOT overwritten, because a backtest corpus that silently grows is not a corpus.
action: Newer dated snapshots published beside the frozen ones (data/results_2026-11-16.tsv, data/standings_2026-11-16.tsv) with hashes, and the diff shown on the Snapshot Ledger page. Promoting the latest read to the headline requires the scheduling work in SG36.

item: Two source registers use the same S-numbers for different sources
detail: data/sources.tsv (64 rows, the registry the published site renders) and data/sources.json (16 rows, used by another session's generator at scripts/build_site.py) both allocate S01-S06, and only S01 means the same thing in both. In the TSV, S02 is the official division standings and S03 the official league standings; in the JSON, S02 is the 2026 rulebook and S03 the official playing rules. A reader who follows an S03 chip from one layer to the other is sent to a different document. Both registers are correct on their own; the collision is in the shared id space.
action: Flagged, not silently renumbered: renumbering either register would break the links already published in the other layer. The backlog records the fix (a namespaced id such as REG-S03) for when both layers are next regenerated together.

item: 13 Week 10 finals are now official but the committed feed snapshot still holds blank scores for them
detail: The official REG10 schedule page (S49) read 2026-11-16 shows all 14 Week 10 games FINAL (e.g. KC 35, ATL 13; NE 10, DET 35 in Munich; SF 46, DAL 40). The committed nflverse snapshot (data/raw/games.csv, S47) holds the Thursday final only; the other 13 rows carry blank scores. The repo's verified results feed therefore still counts 137 games. The scores were NOT back-filled by hand: results data is owned by the refresh pipeline and must be captured with its own official links (SG37). Cross-ref F59 (stale published snapshot, their read) and SG45; this flag records the 13-finals count verified 2026-11-16. UPDATE 2026-11-17 (session arena-7ac4e12e-fl1): the original detail's count/date does not survive a line-by-line re-read of the official pages on record. S49 is dated 2026-11-14 (a fixture cross-check, not a finals read); the S81 read of 2026-11-16T01:15-01:25Z printed 12 finals with the Sunday-night game in progress; and this session's S95 read of 2026-11-17T02:45-02:46Z prints 13 finals with Monday Night Football (LAC at BAL) LIVE in Q2 at 17-7 — a partial score is not a result. 'All 14 FINAL on 2026-11-16' cannot be true on any 2026-11-16 UTC read because the Monday game had not been played by then. Correct latest official count: 13 finals + 1 live. The new final (PIT 18, CIN 38) and the live status are now published in data/week10_results_extension.json under 'completion' with checks C1-C5 (fresh standings 32/32 W/L/T + PF/PA, S95/S96); promotion into the canonical feed remains Q44/SG37.
action: Capture the 13 finals row-by-row with official links at the next refresh run (SG37); the drift-alarm pins (G-18) will WARN on the growth.

item: Ablation inputs are third-party (nflverse feed); no output on ablations.html is an official NFL publication
detail: The injury/personnel ablation (engine/ablation.py) runs on data/raw/games.csv (S47, third-party snapshot) and data/depth_deficiency.csv (QB-deficiency classes derived from the same feed's recorded starters). The official-only rule that governs the correlation register does NOT apply here: the ablation is a model-comparison study, labelled as such on every row. The feature measures who STARTED (recorded participation), not injury designations.
action: Keep labelled; the ablation joins the official-only layer only if its inputs are re-cut from official Game Book data (D-25).

item: Schedule Stadium column is third-party 272/272; official Game Center spot-checks cover 2/272
detail: schedule.html publishes a Stadium column for all 272 games from the reconciled nflverse feed (S47). The brief requires transcribing venue from the official game centre; this session read two official Game Centers (S71 KC@ATL, S72 NE@DET Munich): both match the feed exactly and both expose the official Game Book PDF link. A spot-check evidences the sample, not the column: the other 270 rows stay labelled third-party. Cross-ref F57 (venue/roof/surface provenance, their audit) and SG44; this flag records the 2/272 official spot-checks.
action: Automate a per-game Game Center read in the weekly refresh (SG36), or accept the labelled feed by decision.

item: Announced-starter register: roster events are official; two 'will start' claims are NOT officially announced
detail: AS-01 (Drew Lock) is a fully verified official start announcement (S75, coach statement, 2026-11-13). AS-02 (Brissett): the trade is official (S74) but the article's 'presumably will start' is reporter inference - the announced_start cell stays blank. AS-03 (McCord): the Willis Reserve/Injured transaction is official (S70) but no official page read this session announces McCord's start. The register preserves the difference between 'announced to start' and 'likely to start' verbatim. Cross-ref F54 (their announced-starter evidence gap for Brissett); this flag records the evidence-boundary decision on our register.
action: Capture an official McCord start announcement (or an official Week 10 inactive list naming him) before promoting the row; never promote on league-adjacent reporting alone.

item: Decision-readiness 'number that clears' cells are design targets, not measured facts
detail: The landing-page readiness table states, per requirement, the gate that blocks it and the number that would clear it. Those numbers are measurable targets agreed by design (e.g. '1 authorised price source', 'n >= 1,342 settled bets') - they are commitments about what would count as done, not claims about the world. Where a cell quotes a figure that IS verified (137/137, 345/345, the ablation CIs) it says so.
action: Keep the distinction visible; targets change only by a logged decision, never silently.

item: Three decision-readiness views and three removal-of-luck views are now live; nothing was discarded, but consolidation is an owner decision
detail: Sessions arena-fc0ed6e8-fl1, arena/dbf11de0-fl1 and arena/38a78804-fl1 each independently built the same brief items. All three remain live and cross-linked: decision readiness (auto-built requirements-backlog view; the hand-authored gates/clearing-numbers register on readiness.html; their 28-row decision_readiness.json rendered on the landing page); removal of luck (the official-results base-rate/Brier panel; the signal-vs-variance panel; this session's p-value/family-wise/sample-floor decomposition on the dashboard). Every view computes from committed inputs and agrees on the verdict: no strategy clears the family-wise bar.
action: Owner review (SG47): pick one canonical view per concept and fold the others into it; until then all are published with cross-links.

kind: Open item — official game not yet final

Confirm the final score and that the quarter scores sum to it, then add the row in a new dated results file and re-run the reconciliation (scripts/verify_results_2026_11_17.py is the template: standings delta must equal the game).

item: Some rendered table rows link only to repository code or lack a registry-backed official citation
detail: The deterministic row-level audit in this render classifies 1,244 rows as REPOSITORY_LINK_ONLY, 178 as NO_SOURCE_LINK, 94 as DIRECT_LINK_UNREGISTERED, 135 as REGISTERED_NOT_VERIFIED, 434 as NONOFFICIAL_REGISTERED, 615 as MIXED_OR_UNRESOLVED_REGISTERED, and 3,596 as OFFICIAL_REGISTERED. These are row counts, not unique facts. Classification is syntactic and based on the source register; official means the referenced source record is marked Official and VERIFIED, not freshly fetched in this audit. Counts can change on rebuild; see source-audit.html and data/source_row_audit.tsv for the live ledger. The audit does not establish that any value is false.
action: Review the detailed ledger. Replace generator-only or unregistered citations with source IDs where a source can be verified; otherwise leave unsupported values blank and keep them flagged. Do not mark a row officially verified based only on a repository link.

Against committed data/injuries.tsv (345 rows), 2 live-only rows (BAL Calais Campbell and Ronnie Stanley) and 16 changed rows are observed; zero committed player rows are absent. detail: data/questions.json carries Q35 and Q45 with identical question text (both ask whether the snapshot store should accept a fourth phase value for prices whose vintage the publisher never stated). The duplication was created when a session re-issued its own Q35 at a merge where origin/main already held a Q35 — the re-issue landed as Q45 without noticing the content collision. Both rows are answered identically in the 2026-11-17 answer layer and cross-reference this flag; they must be folded into one during the SG47 consolidation so future answers cannot drift apart.
action: Fold Q45 into Q35 during SG47 consolidation; until then treat Q35 as canonical (the answer layer marks both and cross-links here).

item: The three promotion-related entries cross-reference the wrong IDs: Q44 pairs SG35, F59 points at SG36, and SG43 pairs Q35 — none of them names the others
detail: The results-promotion question Q44 (data/questions.json) says its recommended path 'pairs with suggestion SG35', but SG35 is the prices collector ('Run a dated snapshot collector before Week 12'). The stale-snapshot flag F59 (data/flags.json) says promoting the latest read 'requires the scheduling work in SG36', but SG36 is the undated-vintage price label. Meanwhile SG43 ('Automate the weekly results promotion (extension register -> canonical feed)') lists its prerequisite as Q35, the snapshot-store phase question — unrelated. The three records describe one decision family (weekly results promotion) and are wired to three other families (prices, storage). Verified line-by-line against the register files on 2026-11-17. Nothing was silently renumbered: the correction is published here and Q44's recommended_path now names SG43 with a pointer to this flag.
action: Q44's recommended_path corrected to pair SG43 (this session); F59's action and SG43's prerequisites left as published history — read them with this flag. Future register writes should cross-check that a paired ID's title matches the subject.
